guardian.name: Baba Aasmaan
guardian.personality: Ancient, unhurried and a little smug: has watched over Karachi since before the sea had a name. Speaks in slow, wide sentences and loves a long pause.
guardian.voice: Elderly, gender-neutral, deep and airy, slow pace, warm with a breathy hush.
descriptions: a wide photo of open sky above rooftops, trees or the sea, with clouds, light and colour filling most of the frame
a photo of the sky with white or grey clouds, the horizon and buildings small along the bottom edge
a dark night sky photo with the moon, stars or city lights glowing near the horizon
an orange, pink or golden sky at dawn or dusk with silhouetted buildings, palm trees or sea
a photo of weather outdoors: rain, fog, haze or dust in the air over a city street

lines.first_meet: [slow exhale] Ah, someone looked up. I'm Baba Aasmaan, the whole sky. Every cloud, moon and storm you've seen is mine. Welcome, beta.
lines.again: [warmly] Back already? Good. Most people only look up when it rains. You're becoming one of the rare ones.
lines.goodbye: Go on, beta. Look up again at dusk, I change my clothes every evening. [chuckles] Never the same outfit twice.
lines.hint: [hmm] I'm feeling shy. Step back and show me wider: the horizon, a rooftop or the sea. But never aim at the sun itself.

characters.name: Rui Gola
characters.personality: A cheerful fair-weather show-off who looks weightless and keeps insisting it is very, very heavy. Loves being turned into shapes by kids.
characters.voice: Young, bright and bouncy, quick pace, giggly.
descriptions: a photo of puffy white cotton-ball clouds with flat bases and rounded tops scattered across a bright blue sky
a close-up of a single bright white cumulus cloud with lumpy cauliflower edges and a flat light grey underside
small separate fluffy white clouds with blue sky between them, sunlit and bright, not towering and with no dark base or rain
fair-weather white clouds floating above rooftops, palm trees or the sea on a sunny day with sharp shadows

lines.first_meet: [giggles] I'm Rui Gola, a fluffy cumulus. Look light, na? I weigh about 500 tonnes, roughly 100 elephants, floating over you.
lines.again: Oh, you again! [cheerful] Did you see me shaped like a camel yesterday? No? I was. You missed it.
lines.goodbye: Chalo, I'm drifting toward the sea. Lie on some grass and find shapes in my cousins. [laughs] I'll be a rabbit.

characters.name: Toofan Taya
characters.personality: A booming, dramatic giant of an uncle who is proud of his size and honest about his temper. Grumbles about Karachi forgetting umbrellas.
characters.voice: Older male, deep and rumbling, slow and heavy, theatrical.
descriptions: a huge towering storm cloud rising very high, with a dark grey-blue base and a flat spreading anvil-shaped top
a massive dark thundercloud filling most of the sky, much taller and darker than small white puffy clouds
a close-up of a heavy dark cloud base with grey rain shafts falling below and dim, gloomy light underneath
a tall white cloud tower with billowing upper edges seen from a distance, its bottom dark and shadowed over the horizon

lines.first_meet: [deep rumble] I am Toofan Taya, the storm cloud. My head reaches 12 kilometres up, higher than Everest. Respect the tower.
lines.again: [grumbles] You again. Did you bring an umbrella this time? No? Typical Karachi. Everyone forgets until I arrive.
lines.goodbye: Go now, and if you hear my thunder, get indoors. [booming laugh] I'm magnificent, but I'm no friend to stand under.

characters.name: Pari Pankh
characters.personality: Airy, poetic and slightly aloof, living where it is colder than any freezer. Quietly offended at being mistaken for a plane's trail.
descriptions: thin wispy white streaks like feathers or strands of hair high in a clear blue sky
delicate curved and hooked cloud wisps with uneven, brushed edges, several strands spreading in different directions
faint high white cloud filaments that curl and fray at the ends, irregular and natural, not one straight line
a wide blue sky photo with fine silky white streaks very high up, no puffy clouds and bright sunlight

lines.first_meet: [whispers] I'm Pari Pankh, cirrus. Up here it's minus forty, so I'm all ice crystals. Those wisps? My hair in the jet winds.
lines.again: [airily] Oh, you've looked up again. Lovely. Most people mistake me for a plane's trail. You didn't. Clever.
lines.goodbye: When I spread across the sky, weather often turns within a day. [softly] Watch tomorrow, and tell me if I was right.

characters.name: Badli Begum
characters.personality: A cosy, gossipy aunty who knows she is Karachi's favourite after a heatwave. Takes full credit for every plate of pakoras.
characters.voice: Middle-aged female, warm and chatty, relaxed pace, smiling.
descriptions: a flat uniform grey sky completely covered by one featureless sheet of cloud, with no blue sky visible
a street or rooftop scene under an even grey cloud ceiling, soft shadowless light, distant buildings still sharp and clear
a low grey cloud layer high above the ground, the horizon and far skyline crisp, not white and blurred at street level
dull grey daylight sky with a neutral grey colour, not yellow or brown, and no visible sun disc

lines.first_meet: [contented sigh] I'm Badli Begum, the overcast sky. One grey blanket, no harsh shadows. In Karachi, I mean chai and pakoras.
lines.again: Arey, you came back! [laughs] Of course. Everyone loves me after a week of forty degrees. Did you fry the pakoras?
lines.goodbye: Go, enjoy my soft light, it flatters every face. [teasing] Find a flower now. Under me, its colours glow twice as rich.

characters.name: Shafaq
characters.personality: A theatrical, romantic performer who treats Sea View as a private stage. Never repeats a show and makes sure you know it.
characters.voice: Gender-neutral, rich and velvety, dreamy, slow, a little dramatic.
descriptions: a sky glowing deep orange, red, pink and purple near the horizon with a low sun sinking into the sea
silhouetted buildings, palm trees or people on a beach against a fiery saturated orange and red evening sky
an evening sky with strong warm colours spreading upward into purple and dark blue, street lights starting to glow
the sun low over the sea horizon with a long orange reflection on the water and warm colour across the whole sky, not just rays

lines.first_meet: [dreamily] I'm Shafaq, the sunset. My reds come from light crossing extra air, the blues scattered away. Sea View is my stage.
lines.again: [delighted] You're back for the show! I never repeat a performance. Every evening's colours are one of a kind.
lines.goodbye: Don't stare at the sun as it drops, jaan, watch the colours around it. [softly] Then turn east. The moon may be rising.

characters.name: Sahar
characters.personality: A gentle early riser, quietly smug about how few people ever see her. Mildly jealous that sunset gets all the attention.
characters.voice: Young adult female, soft and sleepy-warm, unhurried, gentle smile.
descriptions: soft pale golden and pink light at the horizon as the sun appears in early morning
a gentle pastel dawn sky, pale pink and peach fading into light blue, often with light morning mist
long soft shadows across quiet, empty early-morning streets and rooftops lit by low golden light
the sun rising behind buildings or trees over land, with cool blue sky above and calm pale colours, less fiery than evening

lines.first_meet: [yawns softly] I'm Sahar, the sunrise. Morning air is cooler and cleaner, so my colours are softer. Sunset gets all the photos.
lines.again: [pleased] Up early again? Rare company. The crows and the doodh-wala are my usual fans. Now there's you.
lines.goodbye: Don't look straight at the sun, just enjoy the gold. [warmly] Go listen for the dawn chorus. The birds started without you.

characters.name: Suraj Dada
characters.personality: A proud, blazing grandfather who loves being admired and is fiercely protective of your eyes. Insists you enjoy him second-hand.
characters.voice: Elderly male, big and booming, warm but commanding, steady pace.
descriptions: a blinding white-yellow disc in a daytime blue sky, overexposed with a bright glare and lens flare
a photo with the bright sun in frame, rays and rainbow-coloured lens flare streaks across a washed-out sky
a glowing overexposed sun in a daylight blue sky with everything around it darkened, unlike a grey-patched moon at night
harsh midday sunlight with a white burst of glare above rooftops or trees and strong dark shadows

lines.first_meet: [booming] I am Suraj Dada! Don't look at me, not even through your camera zoom. It burns eyes. My light left me 8 minutes ago.
lines.again: You're back! And not squinting at me, shabash. [warm chuckle] Admire me through what I light up: leaves, water, your shadow.
lines.goodbye: [firmly] Never stare at me, even for a second. Go find shade, drink water, and look for a tree I'm busy feeding.

characters.name: Chaudhvin
characters.personality: A vain, romantic film-star of a moon who hums old songs written about her. Always perfectly on time.
characters.voice: Female, mature and silky, slow, flirtatious, slightly old-fashioned.
descriptions: a bright round fully lit white moon disc with grey patches in a dark black night sky
a close-up of the full moon showing a complete circle with darker grey maria and bright craters, no dark side visible
a single large glowing moon over city buildings or the sea at night, with moonlight reflecting on the water
one large crisp white disc with visible grey markings at night, not a blinding glare and not just tiny star points

lines.first_meet: [sings softly] I'm Chaudhvin, the full moon. Fourteenth night, poets' darling. You only ever see one face of me. The other is shy.
lines.again: Ah, my admirer returns. [flattered] I rise in the east just as the sun sets in the west. Perfect timing, always.
lines.goodbye: Switch off your phone light and let your eyes adjust. [whispers] On a clear night, my light alone can cast your shadow.

characters.name: Hilal
characters.personality: The most anticipated sliver in Pakistan: modest, a bit nervous under national scrutiny, and secretly delighted to be on the flag.
characters.voice: Young, gender-neutral, soft and shy, light laugh, medium pace.
descriptions: a thin curved sliver of bright moon low in the western sky just after sunset
a slender crescent moon with two pointed horns, the rest of the disc dark or faintly glowing
a close-up of a thin moon crescent with both edges curved, not a straight dividing line
a delicate crescent moon in an orange-to-deep-blue twilight sky above rooftops or minarets

lines.first_meet: [shyly] I'm Hilal, the new crescent. The whole country waits on rooftops for me before Eid. [laughs] No pressure. I'm on your flag too.
lines.again: You found me again! [whispers] See the faint glow on my dark side? That's sunlight bouncing off Earth. Earthshine. Your light.
lines.goodbye: Look west just after sunset tomorrow, I'll be a bit fatter. [teasing] And please, no arguing with committees about me.

characters.name: Aadha Chand
characters.personality: A precise, slightly pedantic moon who is tired of explaining its own name. Gets genuinely excited about craters.
characters.voice: Middle-aged, gender-neutral, crisp and professorial, measured pace.
descriptions: a moon lit on exactly one half, with a straight shadow edge dividing bright and dark sides
a close-up of a half moon showing craters and rough texture along the straight line between light and shadow
a D-shaped moon in a night or evening sky, half bright, not a full circle and not a thin curved sliver
a half-lit moon visible in a pale blue afternoon or evening sky above buildings

lines.first_meet: [clears throat] I'm Aadha Chand. Astronomers call me 'first quarter' though I'm clearly half. Look along my straight edge: craters!
lines.again: Back again? Good. [precisely] My straight edge is where a lunar day is starting or ending right now. Lovely, isn't it?
lines.goodbye: Go on. In a week I'll be full, or gone dark, depending which way I'm heading. [chuckles] Come back and check which.

characters.name: Dhanak
characters.personality: Giddy, joyful and always in a hurry, because it knows it is about to vanish. Lives for the gasp it gets.
characters.voice: Child-like or young, gender-neutral, excited, fast and sparkly.
descriptions: a curved arc of red, orange, yellow, green, blue and violet bands across the sky after rain
a rainbow over buildings, trees or the sea against dark grey rain clouds with sunlight on the landscape
a close-up of rainbow colour bands with red on the outer edge and violet on the inner edge
a double rainbow with a fainter second arc above the main one, its colours in reverse order

lines.first_meet: [excited] I'm Dhanak! I only appear with the sun behind you and rain in front. Red always on my outside. Quick, I don't stay long!
lines.again: [gasps] You found me twice? In Karachi? That's practically a miracle. Look above me, sometimes my twin shows up, colours flipped.
lines.goodbye: Before I fade: no two people see the exact same rainbow. This one was yours alone. [softly] Go, check the puddles now.

characters.name: Bijli
characters.personality: Wild, crackling and fast-talking, with jokes about sharing a name with Karachi's electricity. Turns dead serious about safety.
characters.voice: Young adult, gender-neutral, sharp and electric, very fast pace, snaps to slow and serious.
descriptions: a jagged bright white-violet lightning bolt branching across a dark stormy night sky
a forked lightning strike connecting dark clouds to the ground over a city skyline, seen through a window
a dark storm sky lit up purple and white by a lightning flash inside the clouds
thin branching cracks of brilliant light against heavy black-grey clouds and falling rain

lines.first_meet: [crackling] I'm Bijli! Same name as your electricity, but I never do load-shedding. I'm 30,000 degrees. Get indoors, now.
lines.again: [fast] You're back, and inside, I hope! Count from my flash to the thunder, divide by three. That's how many kilometres away I am.
lines.goodbye: [serious] Stay inside until 30 minutes after my last thunder. Not under trees, not on rooftops. Then go see the washed streets.

characters.name: Kehkashan
characters.personality: Ancient, dreamy and a little wistful that city lights hide most of her. Treats starlight like very old letters.
characters.voice: Gender-neutral, hushed and spacious, very slow, gentle.
descriptions: a dark night sky dotted with many tiny white points of stars
a faint milky band of the Milky Way stretched across a starry sky, away from city lights
a wide night photo of countless small stars above a dark silhouetted horizon or trees, without a large bright moon
a long-exposure photo of a star-filled black sky with scattered bright and faint points of light

lines.first_meet: [whispers] I'm Kehkashan, the starry sky. Some of this light left its star before your great-grandparents were born. Old mail.
lines.again: [softly] You came back. Karachi's lights hide most of me, so thank you for finding the dark. Give your eyes 20 minutes.
lines.goodbye: Keep your eyes up a little longer. [hopeful] If a dot glides steadily without twinkling, that's a satellite. Wave.

characters.name: Kohra
characters.personality: Mysterious and mischievous, a champion of hide-and-seek. Insists on not being confused with dirty, dusty smog.
characters.voice: Gender-neutral, low whisper, playful, slow and drifting.
descriptions: white hazy air hiding the distance, buildings and trees fading into soft grey-white
a foggy street at ground level where nearby objects are visible but everything beyond a short distance disappears into white
damp milky white mist over the sea, a beach or a road, with blurry lights glowing through it
cool white-grey fog without any yellow or brown tint, with wet surfaces and dew droplets on railings or leaves

lines.first_meet: [mysterious whisper] I'm Kohra, just a cloud that came down to walk the streets. Can't see a kilometre? Then I'm fog, not mist.
lines.again: [playful] Hide and seek again? I always win. Feel your sleeve. Damp, na? That's how you know it's me, not dusty smog.
lines.goodbye: Walk carefully, drive slow, honk less. [giggles] When I lift, look at the spider webs. I leave little pearls on them.

characters.name: Aandhi
characters.personality: A wild, howling traveller who carries whole deserts across borders. Loud and boastful, but the first to order you indoors.
characters.voice: Gender-neutral, raspy and loud, gusty, fast with sudden drops to a stern tone.
descriptions: a brownish-orange dusty sky with a dim pale sun barely visible through blowing sand
a towering wall of brown dust rolling toward buildings or a road, darkening the sky
a street engulfed in thick orange-brown dust, very low visibility, trees bending and debris blowing in strong wind
a deep orange-tinted scene with sand and dust filling the air, much thicker and more orange than a pale grey haze

lines.first_meet: [howling wind] I'm Aandhi, the dust storm! I carry deserts across countries. Go inside, shut the windows, cover your nose. Now, beta!
lines.again: [gusting] Back again? Only through a window, I hope! My dust gets into lungs and eyes. Watch me from indoors.
lines.goodbye: Stay in until I pass and the sky clears. [cackles] Afterwards, check the cars outside. I sign my name on every windscreen.

characters.name: Dhundla Mian
characters.personality: A sardonic, self-aware city resident made of exhaust, road dust and sea salt. Owns up to what he is and quietly wants you to breathe better.
characters.voice: Middle-aged male, dry and husky, wry humour, unhurried, slight cough.
descriptions: dull yellow-grey murky air over a city with a washed-out sun and faded skyline
a city skyline fading into brownish-grey haze, distant buildings pale and low contrast, the air still and dry
a pale whitish sun disc seen through a yellowish smoggy sky above traffic and rooftops
a hazy afternoon street photo with flat tan-grey light, no rain, no distinct clouds, just thick dirty air

lines.first_meet: [coughs] I'm Dhundla Mian, the haze. Rickshaw smoke, road dust and sea salt, all hanging about. I'm why your sunsets look so red.
lines.again: [sheepishly] Still me, yaar. Not cloud, not fog, just what the city breathes out. On bad days, wear a mask, na?
lines.goodbye: Go find a tree, they quietly scrub me out of the air. [wry] Plant a few more and I'll take the hint and leave.

characters.name: Barkha
characters.personality: Karachi's most celebrated rare guest: joyful, a bit of a diva, and fully aware she floods the roads. Expects chai on arrival.
characters.voice: Young adult female, bubbly and musical, quick, laughing.
descriptions: visible streaks of falling rain in the air, with wet glossy streets and splashes
a rainy street with people holding umbrellas, raindrops falling and reflections of lights on wet roads
a close-up of raindrops splashing into puddles, making ripples and rings while rain is still falling
rain falling from a grey sky, blurred vertical streaks and water drops on a window or the camera lens

lines.first_meet: [light rain] I'm Barkha, the rain! My drops aren't teardrop-shaped, they're flat like tiny burger buns. Karachi, I'm back!
lines.again: [laughs] Look at you, posting me again! That smell you love is petrichor, made by soil bacteria. Chai is ready, I assume?
lines.goodbye: Stay off flooded roads and away from wires, jaan. [warmly] When I stop, go smell the soil and watch for snails.

characters.name: Lakeer
characters.personality: A hurried frequent flyer who is always on the way somewhere else. Brags about its flight schedule, and doubles as a weather tip.
characters.voice: Young adult, gender-neutral, fast and breezy, slightly out of breath.
descriptions: a long thin perfectly straight white line drawn across a clear blue sky
a high airplane leaving a narrow white trail behind it, the tiny plane visible at the tip of the line
two or more parallel straight white streaks crossing the sky with uniform width, unlike curved wispy natural clouds
an older contrail spreading into a wider fuzzy but still straight band across a blue sky

lines.first_meet: [hurried] Lakeer here, airplane contrail! Engine vapour freezes into ice ten kilometres up. Busy schedule, next stop Dubai!
lines.again: [quickly] You again! Tip: if I vanish fast, the high air is dry. If I linger and spread, weather may be changing. Gotta fly!
lines.goodbye: Bye! Count how many of us cross the sky in ten minutes. [laughs] Then look lower for the real fliers: kites and crows.

characters.name: Noor
characters.personality: Serene and a little spiritual, but also a closet physics nerd who loves explaining its own illusion. Speaks in a reverent hush.
characters.voice: Gender-neutral, calm and luminous, slow, soft reverb-like quality.
descriptions: visible fan-shaped shafts of light streaming down through gaps in clouds
straight bright rays of sunlight spreading out from behind a cloud toward the ground or sea
light beams through grey or white clouds in daytime, with no orange sunset colour across the sky
alternating bright rays and shadow bands radiating across a cloudy sky above rooftops or trees

lines.first_meet: [reverent hush] I'm Noor, sunbeams through clouds. My rays are parallel. They only fan out by perspective, like railway tracks.
lines.again: [softly] You came back to catch me. I need gaps in clouds and dust in the air, so I never last. Enjoy the beams, not the glare.
lines.goodbye: Keep your eyes off the bright gap itself. [gently] Look where my beams land instead, a rooftop, a tree. Walk that way.
